mathematical_checks.topic: Arbitrary finite rational singular-chain model and faces
mathematical_checks.reason: The finite set of occurring simplices is closed under iterated faces. Within each labeled factor, equal parametrized faces get one replacement and homotopy; therefore every formal boundary cancellation remains exact, including rational coefficient cancellations. Extending compatible face homotopies via the existing boundaryless smoothing lemma is valid in increasing dimension. No realization of a chain as an embedded manifold is required.

Preserve the prescribed smooth end collars and truncate below them before using a boundaryless target. For each compact remaining support, its prescribed ambient open neighborhood intersected with the ball interior is a smooth boundaryless target. The smoothing lemma can be used there, and finitely many sufficiently small coordinate perturbations remain there. The finite collar subdivisions can be matched before cancellation, so identical product collar terms cancel and C has compact interior support.

Independent labeled factors allow cutoff-supported Euclidean translations to be submersive in the unfixed region. Fixed lower strata are already transverse; finite compact face data allow smaller relative neighborhoods and perturbations preserving earlier conditions. Finitely many stratum-pair requirements are imposed by the imported map-level parametric and relative theorems. Lower strata of two2chains have dimension less than4 and hence are empty; the surviving complementary intersections are finite with the defined ordered signs.

The interior closed rational2cycle C=P−Pprime bounds a finite continuous rational3chain because H2 of the ball interior is zero. Its formal boundary faces are precisely the prescribed smooth C family, already transverse to fixed Q. The same relative smoothing and facewise perturbation keep C fixed. Products of a3simplex and2simplex have transverse diagonal preimages of dimension1. Codimension1 faces give endpoints; codimension2 faces have expected dimension−1, so no corner endpoints remain. Compactness follows from compact simplex products and the closed diagonal, with the collar/contact regions separated from the boundary.

Outward-normal-first simplex incidence signs and product orientations make identical internal face endpoint sets cancel with the exact opposite total rational boundary coefficients. The surviving first-factor boundary is C dot Q. The second-factor boundary is absent because Z has compact interior support and beta lies on the ball boundary. The map-pair diagonal sign has second-factor dimension2 and is positive, and swapping the two2dimensional factors has sign (−1)^4=+1. Thus the signed compact1manifold boundary identity gives independence in both factors with the asserted linking sign.

The product-collared P and corrected Q meet only above alpha intersect SeifertSurface(beta). The ordered basis (nout,a,s1,s2) computes the same sign as (a,s1,s2) in the boundary orientation. Rational bilinearity then extends from knot components to the full finite cycles without a torsion or embedded-chain restriction.

The two disjoint disk parametrizations give finite continuous chain supports in the standard smooth ball. Their disjoint compact supports have disjoint relatively open ambient neighborhoods. Relative smoothing after collar truncation takes place in those separate smooth opens and fixes the already smooth knot boundaries/collars. The resulting chains remain disjoint, so the supplier gives linking zero. This does not smooth either locally flat disk embedding or require a smooth structure on its normal TOP chart.

In step3.1 the smooth supported chains already meet the model. In step4.2 only the ambient disjoint opens are used as smooth targets; finite continuous TOP-supported chains are replaced by smooth chains within those opens, rational boundary equations admit rational solutions, and fixed collar attachment preserves disjointness. The supplier requires no smooth embedding of the TOP3manifold R. The checked chain output is the same vanishing pairing needed by the existing saturation step.
